info.title: Nova API
info.description: The stardelt Nova gateway: catalog browse, queries and jobs over one identity. In `dev` mode (the default) every route answers without sign-in; in `oidc` mode every described route below requires a session or bearer token except this document itself. Only routes tagged `public` are promised stable.

get.description: Every `Catalog` of the platform namespace, ordered bronze, silver, gold, then the rest alphabetically (`layer`: the `stardelt.io/layer` label, else the catalog's own name): identity, owner, managed access, the storage key prefix, phase and the grants and conditions the access-sync job last wrote. Administrator-only; a non-administrator answers 403 `this view is for platform administrators`. The write is `PUT /api/admin/catalogs/{name}/access`; this route never changes anything. A catalog the job has not observed yet answers `phase: "Unknown"` with no conditions. Without a cluster connection (demo mode, a local run) the answer is the one in-memory `warehouse` catalog. Answers `Cache-Control: no-store`.

200.description: One row per catalog, medallion layers first, then by name

403.description: The caller is not a platform administrator

502.description: The cluster did not answer, or Nova may not list catalogs

put.description: Change one catalog's `spec.owner`, `spec.managedAccess` and `spec.grants` as a JSON merge patch on the `Catalog` resource, carrying the `resourceVersion` the page read. Administrator-only; a non-administrator answers 403 `this view is for platform administrators`. A malformed owner, group name, verb or a duplicate grant is a 400 in the words the form shows; a catalog that changed meanwhile is a 409 `this catalog changed since you opened it; reload`; a name that is not a catalog or no longer exists is a 404; more than 30 changes per administrator in an hour is a 429. Without a cluster connection the answer is 503 `the cluster is not reachable from Nova` (demo mode changes memory instead). Answers the updated row, the same shape as the list, with the new `metadata.generation`; `status.observedGeneration` catches up when the access-sync job runs (about two minutes). Never carries a storage credential. `Cache-Control: no-store`.

200.description: The updated row

400.description: The owner, a group name, a verb or the grant list is invalid

403.description: The caller is not a platform administrator

404.description: No such catalog

409.description: The catalog changed since the page read it

502.description: The cluster did not answer, or Nova may not patch catalogs

503.description: Nova has no cluster client

get.description: The catalogs the caller may browse, each with its Lakekeeper warehouse id and its medallion layer when it has one, plus the catalog a request without `?catalog=` uses. The order is bronze, silver, gold first (in that order), then the rest alphabetically; `layer` is `stardelt.io/layer` from the catalog's `Catalog` resource, else the catalog's own name when that is `bronze`, `silver` or `gold`, and absent otherwise. The list is what the engine's `SHOW CATALOGS` shows the caller (through the caller's own token), minus the engine's own catalogs (`system`, `information_schema`, `memory`, `tpch`, `tpcds`, `jmx`); it is cached for 30 s (the layer for 60 s). Every other `/api/catalog/*` route takes the same `?catalog=`; a catalog the caller may not browse answers 403 there and is never proxied. Empty when no catalog is open to the caller. `demo` in demo mode.

200.description: The browsable catalogs and the default one

502.description: The query engine or the catalog is not reachable

503.description: A catalog the engine lists has no warehouse

get.description: What is in each catalog the caller may browse: schemas, tables, rows, bytes on the object store and the newest commit, plus the sums. Rows are ordered bronze, silver, gold first, then by name, and carry `layer` when the catalog is one of the three (the `stardelt.io/layer` label, else the catalog's own name). The catalog list is the caller's own `SHOW CATALOGS` (`GET /api/catalog/catalogs`); a catalog the caller may not browse is never read and never appears. The numbers come from the catalog's Iceberg metadata (the current snapshot's `total-records` and `total-files-size`), so the endpoint runs no query. They are cached per catalog for 60 s — they describe the catalog, not the person — and at most 200 tables per catalog are loaded: `truncated` says the rows and bytes are a sample while `tables` stays exact. A catalog that cannot be read is listed with zeros and an `error` sentence; only an unreachable engine or catalog fails the request with 502. 403 when no catalog is open to the caller. Never cached by the client.

200.description: One entry per browsable catalog, medallion layers first, then by name, with the totals

403.description: No catalog is open to the caller

502.description: The query engine is not reachable, so the catalogs cannot be named

put.description: Set or remove one column's description. The column must be a field of the current schema, matched exactly. Nova runs `COMMENT ON COLUMN <catalog>.<ns>.<tbl>.<column>` through Trino **as the caller** (source `nova-catalog`), because a column description lives in a new Iceberg schema and only the engine writes it. `?catalog=` picks the catalog. Same 4,000-character limit and null rule as the table description. The interim rule is enforced by Nova; the catalog does not enforce it yet. Demo mode answers 503.

Demo mode answers 503.

put.description: Set or remove a table's description, tags, owner and domain in one Lakekeeper commit. `?catalog=` picks the catalog. Every key is optional: absent changes nothing, `null` (or an empty tag list, or a blank description) removes the property, and a write with nothing to change sends no commit. Description at most 4,000 characters; at most 20 unique tags `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}$`; owner a group name; domain `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,39}$`. An ownerless table may be edited by anybody, but the request must then set `owner` to one of the caller's own groups. **The interim rule is enforced by Nova; the catalog does not enforce it yet** — anyone who reaches Lakekeeper or Trino directly can still change these properties. Edits of one table are serialised by Nova and a contended commit is retried; a catalog that stays busy answers 502 `the catalog is busy, try again`. Demo mode answers 503.

parameters.description: Catalog to work in (`warehouse`, `finance`, …). Omitted, the default catalog is used.

get.summary:
`GET /api/notebooks`: the latest version of every notebook in the caller's groups,
newest first. Administrators see their own groups only.
get.description: The latest published version of every notebook in the caller's groups, newest first. Each row carries the group, the name, the latest `objectVersion`, its size, `uploadedAt` as an RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC (SeaweedFS's RFC 1123 `LastModified` normalised) and the publisher's `uploadedBy` display name. An administrator gets no wider view than their own groups. Unset `NOVA_S3_*` is 503; an S3 that is down or refuses is 502. Answers `Cache-Control: no-store`.

200.description: One row per notebook

401.description: Not signed in

502.description: The notebook store did not answer

503.description: Notebook storage is not configured

put.summary: `PUT /api/notebooks/{group}/{name}`: validate, strip, store one immutable version.
put.description: Publish a notebook as a new immutable object version in the `notebooks` bucket. Needs a signed-in person whose groups include `{group}` (403 `you are not a member of the group <g>`; administrators are not exempt). `{name}` must match `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._ -]{0,127}\.ipynb$` and the body must be an nbformat 4 notebook of at most 5 MiB. Every cell's `outputs` and `execution_count` and the notebook's widget metadata are removed before storing — no cell output reaches the object store. `sha256` is of the stored (stripped) bytes. `parameters` are the `name = literal` lines of the first cell tagged `parameters`, at most 32; defaults are text and are never evaluated. A 61st publish by one person in an hour is 429. Unset `NOVA_S3_*` is 503 `notebook storage is not configured`; an S3 that is down or refuses is 502. Each publish writes one audit line with group, name, version and size, never content.

200.description: The stored version and its parsed parameters

400.description: Bad name or not an nbformat 4 notebook

401.description: Not signed in

403.description: Not a member of the group

429.description: More than 60 publishes in an hour

502.description: The notebook store did not answer

503.description: Notebook storage is not configured

get.description: The published versions of one notebook, newest first, at most 50. Needs a member of `{group}` (403 `you are not a member of the group <g>`; administrators are not exempt). Each row carries the immutable `objectVersion`, its size, `uploadedAt` as an RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC (SeaweedFS's RFC 1123 `LastModified` normalised), the publisher's `uploadedBy` and the `sha256` of the stored bytes. A group with no such notebook answers an empty list. Unset `NOVA_S3_*` is 503; an S3 that is down or refuses is 502. Answers `Cache-Control: no-store`.

get.description: The pipelines the caller may see: their groups' pipelines, and every pipeline for an administrator. A pipeline without `spec.ownerGroup` is administrators-only. `state` is one of `loading`, `paused`, `running`, `failed`, `succeeded`, `idle`; `loaded` is false while Airflow has no DAG for a new pipeline yet. Answers `Cache-Control: no-store`.

post.description: Schedule a statement or a published notebook: create a `Pipeline` for one of the caller's owner groups (`runAs: pipeline-<group>`), validated so the loader accepts it. A body gives exactly one of a non-empty `sql` and a `notebook` (`{ name, objectVersion, params }`, #237) — both or neither is 400 `give a statement or a notebook`. Refusals, in this order: a name outside 1 to 40 lower-case letters, digits and dashes starting with a letter 400; a group the caller is not a member of 403 (`you are not a member of the group <g>` — administrators included); a group without a ready `ServicePrincipal` 409 with the `principals` route's message; an empty, over-20,000-character or NUL-carrying statement 400; a parameter name, a parameter count or value, or a `${…}` placeholder the loader cannot fill 400; a notebook name outside `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._ -]{0,127}\.ipynb$` 400, more than 32 notebook parameters, a value over 256 characters or NUL, or a `params` JSON text over 4096 characters 400, and a version that is not in the store 400 `that notebook version does not exist in group <g>` (503 when `NOVA_S3_*` is unset, 502 when S3 does not answer); a retry, wait, time-limit or run-mode option out of range 400; a cron that is not five in-range fields or fires more often than every five minutes 400; an unknown IANA timezone 400; a name that already exists 409; more than ten creations per user per hour 429. `options` and `params` are optional: an omitted option keeps its default (1 retry after 5 minutes, a 120-minute time limit, `Forbid`); `params` are the statement's `${params.<name>}` values, a notebook's values are in `notebook.params`. Airflow is not needed: the resource is the source of truth, and the answer is the new pipeline with `loaded: false`, `state: "loading"`. The audit line carries the statement's length, the cron and, for a notebook, the group, the file name and the pinned version — never the statement and never a parameter value. Answers `Cache-Control: no-store`.

409.description: No ready principal for the group, or the name is taken

post.description: What the engine says about a statement, without running it: Nova fills the statement's `${run.date}` (today, UTC), `${run.id}` (`check`) and `${params.<name>}` placeholders and sends `EXPLAIN <statement>` to the engine as the caller, under the source `nova-schedule-check`. It never sends `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` and never the statement itself. `checked: false` means this kind of statement cannot be checked here (only `select`, `with`, `insert`, `merge`, `delete`, `update`, `values` and `create … as …` are). A refused statement answers 200 with `ok: false` and the engine's sentence; an engine that does not answer is 502. Refusals before the engine: an empty, over-20,000-character or NUL-carrying statement 400, a parameter table or a placeholder as on create 400. Answers `Cache-Control: no-store`.

200.description: The engine's verdict, or that this statement cannot be checked

400.description: The statement, a parameter or a placeholder is invalid

401.description: No token to sign in with

502.description: The query engine is not reachable

post.description: The next fire times of a cron in its zone, RFC 3339 with that zone's offset (for example `2026-10-21T03:00:00+02:00`), so the Schedule dialog can show what a cadence means before it is saved. A field or a zone as on create (400 with the same sentences); `count` is 1 to 10, 5 when omitted. Like croniter, a day matches when both day fields are restricted and either matches, and when one is unrestricted and the other matches. A wall-clock time the zone skips at a DST jump is not a run; a time that happens twice is answered with its first occurrence. A cron that can never fire answers fewer runs (at most 366 days are searched), not an error. Answers `Cache-Control: no-store`.

200.description: The next runs in the schedule's zone

400.description: The cron, the timezone or the count is invalid

put.description: Change a pipeline Nova created (`app.kubernetes.io/managed-by: stardelt-nova`) and nothing else. A statement pipeline's body carries `sql`; a notebook pipeline's carries `notebook` (`{ name, objectVersion, params }`), and an update never changes which of the two it is: `sql` on a notebook pipeline is 400 `this pipeline runs a notebook`, a notebook on a statement pipeline 400 `this pipeline runs a statement`, and both or neither 400 `give a statement or a notebook`. The body describes the whole editable state: an omitted `schedule` removes it, an omitted `params` removes the table, an omitted option keeps its default, and a notebook body's file name, version and parameters replace the task's `config`. Refusals: a pipeline the caller may not act on 404; a pipeline Nova did not write, or one whose task shape is not exactly one `run` task of kind `sql` or `notebook` 409; the statement, a parameter, a placeholder, a notebook name, a parameter value or count, or a version that is not in the store (503 without `NOVA_S3_*`, 502 when S3 does not answer), an option, the cron or the timezone as on create 400; the group's principal no longer ready 409 with the `principals` route's message; a concurrent change to the resource 409 `the pipeline changed while you edited it: reload`. The audit line carries the statement's length, the cron and, for a notebook, the group, the file name and the pinned version — never the statement and never a parameter value. Answers `Cache-Control: no-store`.

delete.description: Delete a pipeline Nova created. Only a pipeline the caller may act on and that carries `app.kubernetes.io/managed-by: stardelt-nova` may be deleted: a `kubectl` or GitOps pipeline answers 409 instead. Airflow is not called — the resource is the source of truth; the DAG leaves the scheduler's default list after about 90 seconds while its history stays readable. Answers 204 with `Cache-Control: no-store`; the attempt is audited.

Answers the fresh `PipelineView` — the DAG as Airflow returned it after the patch — and `Cache-Control: no-store`. The attempt is audited, including a refusal.

post.description: Start a run now. Nova refuses instead of passing Airflow's silent behaviour on: a pipeline the scheduler has not loaded yet answers 409, a paused pipeline 409 (Airflow would create a run that waits `queued` until someone resumes), more than ten starts per user per minute 429, and a `Forbid` or `Replace` pipeline whose latest five runs include a queued or running one 409 (`Allow` skips that check). `logicalDate` is always now, UTC, whole seconds, so the run has tasks; the note is `Started from Nova by <display name>`. Every attempt, including a refusal, writes one audit line without note text. Answers `Cache-Control: no-store`.

503.description: No cluster connection, or the scheduler is not configured

post.description: Stop a run: mark it failed. This is **not a cancel** — work already in flight can finish and commit its side effects (stardelt-nova#255), so the answer promises only that the run is marked failed. The run id is looked up through this pipeline's DAG id first: a run id of another pipeline answers 404 and is never patched. A run that is not `queued` or `running` answers 409 and is not patched. Answers the fresh `RunView` and `Cache-Control: no-store`. The attempt is audited, including a refusal.

200.description: The run, now failed

401.description: No token to sign in with

404.description: No such pipeline for this caller, or no such run

502.description: The scheduler or the cluster did not answer

503.description: No cluster connection, or the scheduler is not configured

get.description: One page of a task's log: at most 2000 lines and 512 KiB, ANSI escapes removed, the `::group::` source marker dropped (it names internal object-store paths and is never returned). `try` defaults to the task's last attempt; `token` is the `nextToken` of the previous answer. Every read writes one audit line with user, pipeline, run and task — never the content. Answers `Cache-Control: no-store`.

parameters.name: try
parameters.description: Attempt number; defaults to the task's last try

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: Continuation token from a previous answer

200.description: The log page

400.description: `try` is not a positive number

401.description: No token to sign in with

404.description: No such pipeline for this caller, no such run, or no such task

502.description: The scheduler or the cluster did not answer

503.description: No cluster connection, or the scheduler is not configured

AdminCatalog.description:
One catalog, as an administrator sees it.

`displayName`, `description`, `owner`, `keyPrefix`, `warehouseId` and the two
generation numbers are `null` when the resource does not carry them — never
an empty string or a guessed value.

conditions.description: `status.conditions`: what the access-sync job last reported.

grants.description: `spec.grants`, in the order the resource declares them.

keyPrefix.description: `spec.storage.keyPrefix`, or `null` when the catalog uses the lakehouse's defaults.

layer.description:
The medallion layer (`bronze`, `silver`, `gold`) from the `stardelt.io/layer` label
or the catalog's own name; absent for every other catalog (stardelt-nova#109).

managedAccess.description: `spec.managedAccess`: the owner cannot grant on this catalog.

name.description: `metadata.name`: the name users type (`finance.orders`) and the warehouse name.

observedGeneration.description: `status.observedGeneration`: the generation the last sync observed.

owner.description: `spec.owner`: exactly one group. Ownership means `manage`, not `select`.

phase.description: `status.phase` (`Ready` | `Invalid`), or `Unknown` when the resource has no status.

resourceVersion.description: `metadata.resourceVersion`: the version this row was read at.

warehouseId.description: `status.warehouseId`: the Lakekeeper warehouse, as the access-sync job wrote it.

BreakGlassLogResponse.description:
`GET /api/connections/break-glass-log`: the last 200 reads and refusals, newest first. It has
no values by construction (see [`audit::BreakGlassRecord`]).

BreakGlassNotice.description:
The notice an administrator's break-glass read leaves on a group's `Connection` resource and
that the listing shows to the group. It never carries a value.

BreakGlassRequest.description:
`POST …/break-glass` body. No `Debug`: a reason can be sensitive and nothing here should ever
be printed by accident.

BreakGlassResponse.description:
The values, returned once. No `Debug`: the map holds the secret values and is never formatted,
logged or put in an error.

CatalogAccessUpdate.description:
One `PUT /api/admin/catalogs/{name}/access` body.

`resourceVersion` is the value the page read: the API server rejects the merge
patch with `409` when the object changed meanwhile, so two administrators
editing the same catalog cannot silently overwrite each other.

grants.description: The whole `spec.grants` array, each `{group, verb}` once.

managedAccess.description: `spec.managedAccess`: the owner cannot grant on this catalog.

resourceVersion.description: `metadata.resourceVersion` from the row the page holds.

CatalogCondition.description: One condition of a `Catalog`'s status, reduced to the four fields the page shows.

message.description: The sentence the access-sync job wrote, or `null`.

CatalogGrant.description: One declared grant: a group and one verb.

CatalogInfo.description:
One catalog the caller may browse, with its Lakekeeper warehouse id and its medallion
layer when it has one.

id.description: The Lakekeeper warehouse id behind that name.

layer.description:
`bronze`, `silver` or `gold` when the catalog is a medallion layer — from the
`stardelt.io/layer` label on its `Catalog` resource, else from its name. Absent for
every other catalog.

name.description: Catalog name, as the engine and the catalog spell it (`warehouse`, `finance`, …).

error.description:
Why this catalog could not be read — absent for a catalog that was. A sentence,
never URL, token or stack trace.

CatalogMetricsView.description:
One catalog in the answer: the numbers, plus the sentence when the scan failed. A
failed catalog is zeros, never omitted — a page that silently drops a catalog says
"you have none", which is not what happened.

CatalogStats.description: One catalog's numbers, as the endpoint answers them.

lastCommitMs.description: The newest commit among the loaded tables (Unix ms); `null` when none has one.

layer.description:
`bronze`, `silver` or `gold` when the catalog is a medallion layer (see
`crate::catalog::catalog_layers`); absent for every other catalog.

name.description: Catalog name, as the engine and the catalog spell it.

records.description: Rows in the loaded tables' current snapshots.

sizeBytes.description: Bytes the loaded tables' current snapshots occupy on the object store.

tables.description: Tables in the catalog — every one the catalog lists, loaded or not.

truncated.description:
More tables exist than the endpoint loads (200 per catalog): `tables` is exact,
`records` and `sizeBytes` cover the first 200 only.

CatalogsResponse.description:
`GET /api/catalog/catalogs`: the catalogs the caller may browse, the medallion layers
first.

catalogs.description:
Every catalog the caller may browse (`?catalog=` accepts any of these names),
ordered bronze, silver, gold, then the rest alphabetically.

default.description: The catalog a request without `?catalog=` works in.

CheckStatementRequest.description: `POST /api/pipelines/check`: what the engine says about a statement, without running it.

params.description: The parameters the statement's `${params.<name>}` placeholders are filled with.

CheckStatementResponse.description:
The engine's verdict. `checked: false` means this kind of statement cannot be checked here;
`ok` is absent then.

message.description: The engine's sentence when `ok` is false.

ColumnDocumentation.description: One column of the current schema, as the documentation read reports it.

name.description: Field name, exactly as the current schema spells it.

type.description: The field's type as text; a complex type is its JSON text.

ConnectionView.description: One row of `GET /api/connections`. Never carries a value.

oneOf.description: The last break-glass read of a group connection; absent for personal and managed rows.

member.description:
Whether the caller belongs to the scope that owns this row: `true` for a personal or managed
connection and for a group connection of one of the caller's groups; `false` for a group
connection an administrator sees only because they are an administrator. `false` means
read-only for this person — no create, no rotation — except delete and break-glass.

secretKeys.description: The names of the secret fields.

oneOf.description: `Ready` and its reason from the resource's status; absent for a personal connection.

namespace.description: Schema name to create (surrounding whitespace is trimmed).

CreatePipelineRequest.description: `POST /api/pipelines`: schedule a statement for one of the caller's own groups.

oneOf.description: A published notebook version to run instead of a statement (#237).

Retries, the wait between them, the time limit and the run mode; omitted fields keep the
defaults.

params.description:
Values for `${params.<name>}` in the statement; at most 16. A notebook's values are in
`notebook.params`, not here.

sql.description: The statement to run; exactly one of this and `notebook` is given.

DocumentationUpdate.description:
`PUT /api/catalog/tables/{ns}/{tbl}/documentation` body.

Every key is optional. Absent changes nothing; `null` removes the property; an empty tag
list and a blank description also remove. A field whose value equals what the table
already stores is not a change.

tags.description: New tag list (`null` or `[]` removes them).

ErrorResponse.description:
Every non-2xx answer under `/api/` is this envelope (see README "HTTP
conventions"), so every error response in the document points here.

error.description: Human-readable sentence. Never contains tokens, URLs or stack traces.

LogLine.description: One log message. `sources` is deliberately absent: it names internal object-store paths.

LogView.description: One page of a task's log.

admin_console_url.description: `None` in `dev` mode: there is no IdP, so no console.

MetricsResponse.description: `GET /api/catalog/metrics`: what is in each catalog the caller may browse.

catalogs.description:
One entry per catalog the caller may browse: bronze, silver, gold first, then the
rest by name.

generatedAt.description:
When this answer was built (Unix ms). Per-catalog numbers may be up to a minute
older (they are cached).

MetricsTotals.description: The sums over every catalog in the answer. Failed catalogs contribute their zeros.

records.description: Rows in the loaded tables' current snapshots.

sizeBytes.description: Bytes the loaded tables' snapshots occupy.

NamespacesResponse.description: Iceberg `ListNamespaces` result: each namespace is a list of levels.

NewConnection.description:
`POST /api/connections` body. `secret` holds the values; they are written to the store and
never returned.

secret.description: The secret field values. Write-only: Nova stores them and never reads them back.

default.description:
The default as the cell would run it: a string literal without its quotes, any
other literal exactly as written. Never evaluated.

NotebookRequest.description:
The published notebook version a schedule pins (#237): the `.ipynb` file name, the immutable
object version a publish answered, and the parameters the run passes to papermill.

name.description:
`<group>/<name>` is the object key; the group is the pipeline's `ownerGroup`, so a
notebook of another group can never be named.

objectVersion.description: The S3 object version, never a branch or a tag: exactly the bytes a person published.

params.description:
Parameter values by name; at most 32, names `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,63}`, values up to
256 characters. Written as the task's `config.params` JSON object string.

uploadedAt.description:
The version's `LastModified` as RFC 3339 in UTC (`2026-10-21T01:24:28.000Z`),
whichever of S3's two date shapes the gateway answered.

uploadedBy.description: The `x-amz-meta-uploaded-by` the publisher wrote (their display name).

uploadedAt.description:
The version's `LastModified` as RFC 3339 in UTC (`2026-10-21T01:24:28.000Z`),
whichever of S3's two date shapes the gateway answered.

OidcMe.description:
`/api/me` in `oidc` mode: claims, never tokens. Nova still talks to Trino and
Lakekeeper with its service connection, and says so (`identity_forwarding`).

admin_by.description: `"group"` or `"role"`: which of the two `admin_group` is. `None` with it.

admin_console_url.description: Realm admin console derived from the issuer; `None` for non-Keycloak issuers.

admin_group.description:
The configured value behind this caller's administrator decision: the group
matched, or the role held (and the configured precedence for a member). `None`
when neither is configured (#213).

session_expires_at.description:
Unix seconds at which the browser session can no longer be renewed and the
person signs in again; `None` for an Authorization-header call, which has no
session. Never the access token's own `exp`.

options.description:
Retries, the wait between them, the time limit and the run mode as the resource carries
them, with the defaults filled in when a field is absent.

PipelineDetail.description:
`GET /api/pipelines/{namespace}/{name}`: the view, the latest runs and the resource's
parameters, retry policy and options.

PipelineOptions.description:
The advanced options of a schedule (#223), all optional: an omitted field keeps today's
default (one retry, five minutes between retries, a two-hour time limit, one run at a time).
`Replace` is deliberately not offered — the loader treats it as `Forbid`.

backoffMinutes.description: The wait between attempts, 1 to 60 minutes.

concurrency.description: `Forbid` (one run at a time, the default) or `Allow` (runs side by side).

retries.description: Extra attempts after a failure, 0 to 5.

timeoutMinutes.description: The longest a whole run may take, 1 to 720 minutes.

PipelineOptionsView.description: The options as the resource carries them, defaults filled in — what the edit dialog prefills.

PipelineView.description: One pipeline in the list: the resource plus what Airflow says about it.

createdAt.description:
`metadata.creationTimestamp` as the cluster wrote it (RFC 3339); `None` for a malformed
resource.

loaded.description: `false` while Airflow has no DAG for the resource yet; the loader needs about 25 seconds.

schedule.description: The cron schedule, with the time zone in parentheses when there is one.

state.description:
`loading`, `paused`, `running`, `failed`, `succeeded`, `idle`, or `not-loaded` after three
minutes without a DAG.

PreviewScheduleRequest.description: `POST /api/pipelines/preview-schedule`: the next fire times of a cron in its zone.

count.description: How many runs to list, 1 to 10; 5 when omitted.

runs.description: The next fire times in the schedule's zone, RFC 3339 with that offset.

PrincipalView.description: One of the caller's groups and its pipeline principal.

message.description:
`null` when ready; otherwise the `Ready` condition's message, or `no status yet`, or the
`make sync-principal` command for a group without a principal.

principal.description: `pipeline-<group>` when such a `ServicePrincipal` of this group exists.

objectVersion.description: The immutable S3 version id a schedule pins.

sha256.description: Lower-case hex SHA-256 of the stored bytes (outputs already stripped).

RetriesView.description: The retry policy of a pipeline.

RotateRequest.description:
`PUT …/secret` body: the field values to write. Write-only, like the create body, and never
printed — no `Debug` on purpose.

secret.description: The fields to rotate; a managed connection sends every field.

RunResponse.description: `GET …/runs/{run_id}`: one run and its task instances.

RunView.description: One DagRun. `type` is Airflow's `run_type` under the name the UI uses.

ScheduleRequest.description: A cron expression and its IANA zone; both required when a `schedule` object is sent.

TableDocumentation.description: The documentation of one table, plus what the caller may do with it.

canEdit.description: Whether the interim rule lets this caller edit (see the module docs).

columns.description: The fields of the **current** schema, in schema order.

editRule.description: One sentence for a person: why `canEdit` has the value it has.

owner.description: The `stardelt.owner` property: a group name, or `null`.

tags.description: The `stardelt.tags` property, split on commas, trimmed and sorted.

TableMetadataResponse.description:
Iceberg `LoadTable` result: where the metadata lives plus the metadata
document itself (schema, partition specs, properties). The metadata body
is the catalog's own document — Nova never reshapes it.

TaskSpecView.description:
One task as the resource declares it. A `sql` task's statement and a `notebook` task's file
name, version and parameters are carried only by the detail route (Schedule's edit dialog
prefills from them).

notebook.description: The `.ipynb` file name of a `kind: "notebook"` task (#237).

notebookParams.description: The parameters a notebook task passes, parsed back from `config.params`.

objectVersion.description: The immutable object version a notebook task pins.

TaskView.description: One task instance of a run.

UpdatePipelineRequest.description:
`PUT /api/pipelines/{namespace}/{name}`: change the statement, the schedule, the parameters
and the options — or, for a notebook pipeline, the notebook, its version and its parameters.
Every other field of the resource stays as it is, and what the pipeline runs never changes
kind.

oneOf.description:
The notebook, its version and its parameters for a notebook pipeline; a statement
pipeline refuses it.
The whole option set; omitted means the defaults.

params.description: The whole parameter table; omitted means none.

oneOf.description: Omitted means no schedule: the pipeline then runs on demand only.

sql.description: The statement of a statement pipeline; a notebook pipeline refuses it.

WarehouseInfo.description:
OpenAPI shapes for the catalog routes (first slice of ticket #107).

Nova proxies these bodies — from Lakekeeper upstream, or from the
in-memory demo shapes in `demo.rs` — so the structs below mirror the
proxied Iceberg REST shapes rather than being constructed anywhere.
`#[schema(rename = …)]` keeps the hyphenated Iceberg field names.

id.description: The Lakekeeper warehouse id, or `"demo"` in demo mode.

tags.name: public
tags.description: Stable surface for tools and scripts. Breaking changes bump `info.version`.

tags.name: internal
tags.description: UI-only surface. May change or disappear without notice; do not build tools on it.
